note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the very first full build of the piece.
note.changing: The whole composition goes down at once: the coiled silver body, a flame running along its fin, a fan of crest rays above the head, round chrysanthemum and eye motifs packed into the pockets, strange script along the body, and the name riding the bottom coil.
note.why: The serpent's coil gives the circle a strong spine and frames pockets to fill, while the flame along its outer edge fills the rim of the badge.
note.idea: The giant oarfish is the longest bony fish in the sea, a silver ribbon with a blood-red crest that sailors took for a sea serpent, so the artist lets it be one: the head sits near the center with a portal eye, the ribbon body coils around the badge like an ayahuasca serpent, its red dorsal fin burns as one continuous flame along the outside of every coil, and the tail curls into a nautilus spiral, with chrysanthemums, eyes and liquid spirals in the pockets and rainbow echo bands wrapped around everything.

note.saw: The head read as a bullet with a flat back, the crest as a stiff orange comet tail, the body as a strip of film, and the name was shouting in all caps with a 3D extrusion.
note.changing: Rebuilds the head as a blunt oarfish profile with a bigger eye, widens the body, adds eight new motif designs, and rewrites the name as SavesFish in cream letters on a calm dark cartouche carried by the swollen bottom coil. A hidden math error slips in too, flooding the inside of the coil with flat cream.
note.why: SavesFish asked for that exact spelling and for the name to read instantly, so it gets a quiet dark backing built into the serpent's own body while the art stays wild everywhere else.

note.saw: The head still looked like a tin can with straight stripes across it, and the crest like a feather duster.
note.changing: Scales the head up with a rounder forehead, pearly ripples spreading out from the eye, crescent gill covers trimmed with red flame, little scale-eyes on the cheek, and an almond mask with lashes around a bigger spiral portal eye. The crest is rebuilt as wavy red flame tresses.
note.why: The eye is the focal point of the whole badge, so the face should ripple outward from it like a pond around a dropped stone.

note.saw: Between the motifs the bands had clumped into flat blobs, thick cyan, olive and pink triangles, because only one or two bands fit in each gap.
note.changing: Opens more room between the motifs so four to six thin echo bands wrap every shape, and calms the wobble in the field; the crest leans further toward red. The body is still a plain white tube for now.
note.why: Many thin halos read as rippling liquid, while a few thick ones read as stained glass, the opposite of the dense rainbow echoes the artist was after.

note.saw: The deep bands in the field had turned olive and brown, and a black dead zone surrounded the crest because the field stopped well short of the flames.
note.changing: Swaps the deep bands for cool violet, plum, indigo and teal, and lets the field flow right up to the crest. The crest itself is unchanged in this pass.
note.why: Olive and brown were muddying the rainbow; cool darks between the bright bands keep every color clean and frame the fire instead of leaving a dead ring around it.

note.saw: The crest finally read as fire, even at thumbnail size. But the tail spiral was a tangle whose inner turns overlapped and crossed patterns, a dark hollow opened inside the arc of the front flames, and up close the bright bands had no fine detail.
note.changing: The tail spiral now makes one clean turn and ends in a small glowing jewel, motifs are allowed to sit inside the hollow of the flames, and every bright band gets a fine dark hairline down its middle.
note.why: A spiral only feels hypnotic when you can follow it with your eye, and the hairlines give the bands the hand-inked outline, gap, outline rhythm of the reference painting.

note.saw: The tail still tangled: the center of its spiral sat almost on top of the body coming in from the ring, so the curled tip landed on the coil itself.
note.changing: Moves the spiral inward so the tail curls into the open pocket above the head, narrowing into one whip-thin turn that ends in its jewel. The crest's flames now stream back over the neck instead of shooting straight up, which frees the space the tail needs.
note.why: Real oarfish crests stream backward along the body, and a thin tail coiling into a jewel reads like the end of a breath rather than a knot.

note.saw: The tail curls cleanly, the crest streams back like a real flame plume, and the whole badge reads at a glance. What it lacked was beings: nothing in the pockets looked back except small eyes, and the center had no real light.
note.changing: Two alien faces with huge slanted almond eyes, a third eye and a jester crown of flame points join the pocket motifs; small eyes ride inside the dorsal flame; curling smoke tendrils with sparks peel off it; and a soft starburst of light radiates from the oarfish's eye.
note.why: DMT visions are famously inhabited, with beings watching from the walls, so the serpent should swim through a crowd of watchers, lit from its own eye.

note.saw: The new light beams washed the motifs right of the head into haze, both faces landed badly (one half off the left edge, one under the haze), the echo bands were mostly purple and cyan, and the name cartouche ended in blunt squares.
note.changing: Softens the beams, moves the faces into pockets inside the badge, steps the echo bands through a full rainbow outward from every shape (cyan, magenta, gold, emerald, violet, orange) with cool deep bands between, and gives the cartouche rounded scroll ends with more breathing room.
note.why: Each shape should radiate its own rainbow halo like the reference painting, and the beings need to sit where you can meet their eyes.

note.saw: Up close the faces looked lumpy and their eyes were thin slits, and long dark crimson tails with heavy outlines made a smoky, murky patch at the top of the crest.
note.changing: Redraws the beings as classic visitors: a smooth domed head with a pointed chin, glossy black almond eyes with reflections, a jester crown of five curling bell-tipped points, cheek spirals and a third-eye portal. The crest's inner flames reach further toward each tip, its outer layer turns a brighter crimson, and its outlines thin.
note.why: The watching beings are the emotional hook of a DMT trip, so their eyes must read as eyes at a glance; and fire should glow, not smoulder.

note.saw: The crest now glowed from crimson edge to white-hot core, but the visitors' eyes tilted the wrong way, inner corners up, so they looked sleepy and sad instead of uncanny.
note.changing: Flips the slant so the outer corners sweep upward, and makes the black almond eyes fuller.
note.why: That upward outer slant is what makes a visitor's gaze feel ancient and knowing; a few degrees decide whether a face watches you or dozes.

note.saw: The visitors finally looked back with that uncanny slant and the name read instantly at small badge size. One thing still jarred: the pectoral fin behind the gill looked like a red claw of separate strokes.
note.changing: Turns the pectoral fin into a translucent red fan with dark ray lines and golden highlights, matching the rest of the flame family. This is artist 1's final frame.
note.why: Every fin on this fish is fire, so even the smallest one should belong to the same flame.

note.saw: Artist 1 had finished: a coiled silver serpent with a burning crest, watching visitors and a name that reads instantly.
note.changing: Nothing yet. The second artist renders artist 1's final exactly as it stands, as a starting point to study before touching anything.
note.why: A takeover starts with an honest look: the new artist saved the draft untouched and listed its six biggest weaknesses, from the lack of light and depth to the flat name block, before planning a rewrite.
note.idea: Rebuild the piece from scratch as a lit hyperspace: a liquid marbled field of swirling rainbow bands with a glowing hex-lattice tunnel inside the coil, and an unmistakable oarfish at its heart, with a steep-browed head, a crest of separate crimson flame streamers, a chrome-silver ribbon body, a breathing flame fin and jeweled oars, while the name moves onto a flowing banner that wraps the bottom coil.

note.saw: With fresh eyes, artist 1's final sat on one flat plane: no light, no depth, a field of identical round button blooms, a pale lavender tube for a body, a tin-can head under an orange fan drifting toward a betta fish's tail, two dead-straight red wires for oars, and a big flat navy sticker for the name.
note.changing: A full rebuild. The field gets a first try at marbling, with eyes opening where loops close; a glowing hex tunnel opens inside the coil; the fish gets a real oarfish head with a big round portal eye, a crest of separate crimson streamers, a chrome-silver body with dark oblique streaks carrying eyes, and wavy pearl-strung oars with eye-leaf paddles. The name moves onto a banner around the bottom coil in neon-tube letters.
note.why: DMT space is lit from within and pulls you in, so the piece needs a light source and a tunnel, not just pattern; and the fish has to be unmistakably an oarfish, the silver sea serpent with the burning crown.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's swimming, pearl-strung oars and its slow breathing wave for the dorsal flame; the dead maroon cave it pointed out vanished with the rewrite, and its idea of glyphs drifting to a visitor waited until the visitors found their places.

note.saw: The new world worked, but the banner was a huge navy slab hiding the whole bottom coil, the flame fin ran along the inner side of the right coil, the field was a hundred purple discs of one size, and the tail ended thick like a cane handle.
note.changing: The round's fixes, built just before the app crashed, are rendered on resume: a slim banner, flames on the outer edge of every coil, field discs shrinking toward the rim, a whip-thin tail, sheen bands and a braided line along the body. But the picture comes out as an empty navy square.
note.why: The tunnel under the chin should be the sun of the piece, so the world around it has to catch its light and fall away toward an edge you can never reach.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's rainbow sheen bands, braided lateral line and river of stars along the spine, plus its tunnel rim light, shrinking field and whip tail.

note.saw: With the picture back, the field was the weak part: a grid of round coins, each in a dark disc with the same blue ring, packed edge to edge. It was the opposite of loose and fluid, and at badge size it read as bubble wrap.
note.changing: Rebuilds the field as liquid marbling: every motif spins the liquid around it into a whirlpool, counter-turning whirlpools open in the seams, motifs are fewer and further apart, and almond eyes and paisleys drift in the current, turned along the flow. The bands pale toward the tunnel's light, and the lower oar is shortened so its paddle rests on the tunnel floor, leaving ripple rings.
note.why: A sea serpent should swim through something that moves; marbled whirlpools turn the background from wallpaper into a current the oarfish stirs as it coils.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's shorter oar and ripple rings, since an oar dipping into liquid light should leave rings, and saved its forked crest tips for the next round.

note.saw: The field flowed, but now the fish looked stiff inside it: the head was a chrome bullet with four dark crescents across the back like a tin-can lid, a mud-brown wall behind the crest drank the fire's light, and one whirlpool ended in a flat lime-green blob.
note.changing: Gives the fish a real oarfish head, deep at the nape with a near-vertical forehead the crest grows from, a short rounded snout and the portal eye set forward, with its rainbow rings rippling down the neck and a gold gill line carrying five tiny eyes. A glowing membrane, amber to crimson to magenta, now joins the streamers, the tallest tips fork into ember-tipped hairlines, a small eye looks up from the tunnel's white-gold heart, and the ribbon swells and narrows in a slow wave.
note.why: Sailors called the oarfish the king of herrings because of that crown, so it has to burn and glow, not smoulder; and the light at the end of the tunnel should never be empty, but someone looking back at you.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's seamless head, forking flame tips and eye in the tunnel's core, but made the crest veil glow solid instead of see-through, because crimson glass over teal bands turned brown all over again.

note.saw: The crest glowed and the head flowed into the ribbon, but the rebuilt field had lost its beings, so the snout pointed into an empty room. Gold rivets sat dead still in the pouring ink, cream curls lay scattered like confetti, orange ink near the fire competed with the flame, and some band edges looked like torn paper.
note.changing: The beings return: a jester-crowned visitor at the top, a ghost face beside the snout drawn only with lines of light so the marbling flows straight through its head, and a second visitor beneath it like a totem. Strings of beads now pour into every whirlpool, shrinking from gold to a white spark, the roomiest whirlpools open an eye, the field's orange turns rose, and every band edge is smoothed to silk.
note.why: In a DMT space the beings don't walk in from somewhere else, they condense out of the pattern, and a face half seen in moving water is more uncanny than one painted on a coin; the bead trails give the eye a path into every vortex.
note.visionary: Took all three of the Visionary's offers: beads pouring into the whirlpools, a being condensing out of the bands beside the snout, and cooling the orange ink so only the serpent burns.

note.saw: Only one real chrysanthemum was left in the field, the oarfish and the ghost beside its snout were face to face but silent, and up close the ends of the name banner were flat, empty navy.
note.changing: Chrysanthemums now bloom among the middle-sized motifs all over the field, and the spirals drop a level of buds too small to see. Four runes drift out of the oarfish's mouth along a dotted gold arc and dive into the ghost's third eye, and the banner gets a quiet starfield and a gold scroll curl in each end, well clear of the letters. This is the finished piece.
note.why: The chrysanthemum is the doorway image of the breakthrough, so it should keep blooming wherever you look; and DMT beings famously speak in visible language, so a line of glowing script turns the meeting of fish and ghost into a conversation.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's oldest open offer, glyphs drifting from the mouth into a visitor's third eye, now that a visitor finally sits beside the snout.

visions.seen: That spiral pupil has swallowed me and I'm falling down it while the crest roars like a solar flare, the purple visitor leans in close, and the new golden fan fin under the gill flutters like a moth wing. But two red wires hang dead straight from the jaw like unplugged cables, and behind the fire there's a silent maroon cave where hyperspace hasn't finished loading.
suggestions: **The oars, lower center** (the two red filaments running from under the jaw to the eye-tipped leaves near x 330, y 535 and x 385, y 585 in the 800 px render; halve for the 400 box). Right now they are straight wires of even width. I see them as the true oars of the oarfish, swimming: each one could undulate in a slow sine (2 or 3 gentle waves along its length) and taper from about 4 px at the root to 1.5 px. Thread 4 or 5 glowing pearls along each, shrinking and shifting from gold to white toward the tip, and give each eye-leaf paddle two thin contour echoes (cyan, then magenta). In hyperspace nothing hangs dead straight. Every tendril breathes, and strung jewels are that place's native language. The tips already sit well clear of the cartouche's gold rim, so keep them there.

**The maroon cave behind the crest, upper left** (the flat dark crimson patch around x 220 to 330, y 100 to 300, between the flame tips and the field). I see the crest's smoke curdling into a ghost chrysanthemum there: one ring of 12 to 16 pointed petal outlines in gold and rose at about 30% opacity, centered near (265, 200) with a radius of 50 to 60, drawn behind the flame tongues. Inside it goes a smaller ring turned half a petal, with a tiny eye at its heart. The jeweled chrysanthemum unfolding out of smoke is the breakthrough moment itself, and it turns a dead zone into depth without stealing light from the fire.

**The gap between the snout and the purple visitor, right of the eye** (from the mouth near x 518, y 345 to the visitor's third eye near x 590, y 302). The fish and the being are face to face but silent. Let 5 to 7 of the body's own rune glyphs drift out of the mouth along a faint gold dotted arc and into the visitor's third eye, shrinking from about 9 px to 4 px as they go, just over the light beams. The beings in there speak in visible, self-shaping language. This turns the meeting into a conversation and stitches the two focal points together.

**The dorsal flame along the bottom and left rim** (the orange fringe outside the cartouche, y 690 to 770 at the bottom). Here it reads as even roof shingles with straight ray lines, while the crest is wild fire. Let the tongue lengths breathe in a slow wave around the coil: every fifth or sixth tongue grows longer, with a curled tip like a crest flame, and the others shrink so everything stays inside the current rim. Bend the straight ray lines into gentle S-curves. Then one living flame really runs from crown to tail. All of this stays outside the gold rim, so the name keeps its calm backing.
visions.keep: The calm navy cartouche with the cream SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim. It reads instantly in the 240 px test, so nothing new should touch it. Also keep the spiral portal eye and its light beams, the crest's crimson to white-hot fire streaming back over the neck, the clean single-turn tail spiral ending in its jewel, the two visitors with their upward-slanted eyes, and the new translucent golden fan pectoral fin, which finally belongs to the flame family.

visions.seen: Render #94 is the very same frame as #90, so I've stared down that spiral pupil until the walls breathe on their own, and now I see the one thing still asleep is the serpent's silver skin: one even lavender mesh from neck to tail, snagged by stray rainbow wires. Vision 1's four offers still hang there unopened; these are new ones to sit beside them.
suggestions: **The silver skin, the pale lavender scale bands along the whole coil** (from the neck near x 300, y 390 in the 800 px render, around the left loop at x 60 to 200, up the right side at x 640 to 740, to the tail curl near x 490, y 175; halve for the 400 box). Right now it is one even mesh of one size. I see real oarfish silver turning to liquid chrome: 8 to 10 soft sheen bands laid across the body, each about 26 px wide and square to the spine, filled with a cyan to violet to rose to gold gradient at 20 to 28% opacity, spaced a little closer each time, like a wave of light rolling toward the tail. Let the mesh cells shrink as well, from about 9 px at the neck to 4 px at the tail curl. In hyperspace silver is never gray, it is oil-slick rainbow, and scales that shrink along the coil make the serpent fall away into infinity instead of lying flat. The bands end where the body slips under the cartouche's gold rim, so the name keeps its calm.

**The stray rainbow wires crossing the body** (the slanted cyan, lime and magenta hairlines that cut across the navy lane near x 105 to 140, y 435 to 485 and x 205 to 240, y 335 to 375 on the left, and x 590 to 720, y 505 to 550 lower right). They cross at random angles and read as tangled cable. I see them gathered into the oarfish's lateral line as a braid: three strands (cyan, magenta, gold), each a slow sine of the same period but shifted a third of a wave from the next, hugging the inner edge of the navy lane from just behind the gill to the tail curl, with a 2 px break in a strand wherever another passes over it. Energy in that realm travels in helices and braids, never in loose wires, and one living current from gill to tail makes the whole coil a single creature.

**The big chrysanthemum mandala inside the coil, right of center** (centered near x 565, y 440, radius about 68). It sits perfectly still, every petal pointing straight out. I see it begin to turn: rotate each petal ring a little further than the ring inside it (inner ring 0°, then +7°, +14°, outer ring +21°) so the petals line up into soft spiral arms, and draw a 3-turn gold hairline spiral inside its blue center disc. The spinning jeweled chrysanthemum is the doorway image of the breakthrough, and a whorl beside the spiral eye gives you two portals that rhyme. Its outline and size stay exactly as they are.

**The empty navy stretches of the rune lanes** (left lane near x 105 to 140, y 500 to 555; right lane near x 680 to 720, y 290 to 380; anywhere the lane runs 40 px or more without a glyph). The runes sit there like chalk on a blackboard. I see the lane as a night river: 1 to 1.5 px star dots in white, cyan and pale gold at about 50% opacity, thickest along the lane's centerline and thinning toward its edges, and every rune given a soft halo of its own color (a blurred copy behind it, stdDeviation 1.5, 55% opacity). Over there the script is written in light, not ink, and glowing glyphs in a river of stars turn the serpent's spine into the channel the language flows through. Stars stay inside the lanes, never in the cartouche.
visions.keep: The calm navy cartouche with the cream SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim, which still reads instantly at 240 px. Also keep the spiral portal eye and its soft beams, the crest's crimson to white-hot fire, the clean one-turn tail curl and its jewel, both visitors with their upward-slanted eyes, the golden fan pectoral fin, the yellow chevron stitching along the inner edge of the coil, and the full-spectrum halo echoes around every shape in the field.

visions.seen: The whole world has been rebuilt around me. A hex tunnel just opened under the oarfish's chin and its white-gold core is breathing at me, the oars swing on pearls down into it, and a flame fringe licks along the rising body. Then I look up, and the field is a hundred purple coins of the same size in the same light, as if nobody told them the sun had moved into the tunnel.
suggestions: **Light from the tunnel core, falling on the field and the fish** (the core sits near x 400, y 490 in the 800 px render; halve for the 400 box). Right now the core glows but nothing around it catches the light. I see every field disc within about 350 px of the core lit on the side that faces it: an arc of the disc's own outline, about 80° wide and centered on the direction to the core, stroked cream-gold (#FFF3C4 into #FFD23F) at 2 to 3 px, with a blurred copy underneath (stdDeviation 3), and opacity falling from about 0.8 for the nearest discs to 0 at 350 px. The same warm rim could run along the underside of the head and jaw (x 400 to 520, y 395 to 410) and the lower edge of the crest. In hyperspace the light comes from inside the place, and once the walls catch it the tunnel becomes the true sun of the piece. Leave the banner and the letters out of it completely.

**The disc field, all four corners and the whole rim** (the round chrysanthemum discs, which are nearly all one size and one magenta-violet). I see the field turning into a hyperbolic plane, like Escher's Circle Limit: pack the discs with a radius cap that shrinks with distance d from the badge center (400, 400), roughly r_max × (1 − (d/400)²) with a floor near 10 px. They stay big near the fish and crowd smaller and smaller toward the edge, and the outermost ones deepen toward indigo. The badge is a circle, so the rim becomes an edge you can never reach, and that endless curving-away is how hyperspace's walls feel. It touches only field discs, never the banner.

**The tail crook, upper right** (the silver tube rising at x 600 to 660, y 150 to 470 and hooking left to its blunt end near x 530, y 205). It stays as thick as the body all the way and stops like a cane handle. I see the real oarfish whip: from about y 300 upward the tube narrows to 5 or 6 px, then winds about 1.5 turns, tighter each turn, around a center near (560, 200). Its dark streaks shrink to dashes, the flame fringe thins to single sparks, and it ends in an 8 px jewel eye. A spiral you can follow to its vanishing point pulls the eye inward forever, and it frees the purple pocket the crook was closing off. (Artist 1's one-turn tail jewel, coming back whip-thin.)

**The seam between head and body, left of the eye** (the dark vertical edge near x 345, y 300 to 410, where the silver head meets the striped tube like a can lid). I see the rainbow ripples that spread out from the eye carried straight over that seam: soften the dark seam stroke to a hairline and let 4 or 5 of those orange, red and blue contour lines run on another 80 to 120 px along the body, bending with its flow and fading to 0. A thin gold-edged gill crescent with a row of 5 tiny eyes could sit where the seam was. Over there, skin is one continuous field of waves with no parts bolted together, and this lets the eye's pond ripple down the whole serpent.
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline. It reads instantly in the 240 px test, so keep everything new off it. Also keep the hex tunnel and its white-gold core, the spiral portal eye with its gold sunburst lashes, the oars hanging on their pearls with the eye-leaf paddles (Vision 1's oars, taken), the breathing flame fringe along the rising body (Vision 1's dorsal wave, taken), the eye-tipped petals on the chrysanthemums, and the dotted maroon channels with the little green eye-triangles between the discs.

visions.seen: The lights went out. Render #113 (and the #112 test before it) is pure navy void with one tiny broken-picture glyph in the top-left corner, and the oarfish has slipped through the floor of hyperspace. The last frame I can still see, test #109, had the field cooled to a deep teal marble with an eye at the heart of every mandala, and that is the frame I'm dreaming on below.
suggestions: **The void itself: the blurred glow behind the runes in the body lanes** (the first glyph of that glow sits on the neck lane near x 370, y 340 in the 800 px render; halve for the 400 box). I can see you took Vision 2's glowing script, and the light is real, but the glow layer's group tag writes its stroke width twice, 0.9 and then 2.2. A browser refuses the whole picture over one repeated attribute, so every render since midnight has come out as empty navy. I see only the 2.2 kept, for the wider, softer halo, and the whole serpent coming back at once with its runes lit from behind. Nothing else needs to change. Even the elves can't paint on a canvas that won't open.

**The lower oar paddle, just above the "s" and the "F"** (the eye-leaf near x 418, y 578 in #109, which hangs past the tunnel's lower edge onto the banner's dark top). I see the oar ending about 30 px shorter, so the paddle rests on the tunnel's hex floor clear of the banner. Where each paddle touches the floor, two or three thin ripple ellipses could spread out flat in the tunnel's perspective, about 0.6 px, cyan then violet, widening and fading from 0.7 to 0 opacity. In there the floor is liquid light, and an oar dipping into it should leave rings. It also gives the letters back their whole calm backing.

**The tips of the crest, upper left of center** (the tallest crimson streamers, about x 240 to 340, y 70 to 180 in #109, each ending in one rounded tongue with an ember dot). I see the last 15 to 20 px of the five or six tallest streamers forking: one tongue into two hairlines, and each of those into two more, thinning from about 1.2 to 0.5 px and running crimson to gold to white. The four new tips each carry a tiny ember and stay inside the crest's present outline. Fire that branches into smaller copies of itself is how the patterns over there grow, and it makes the crown look like it is still being drawn as you watch.
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline, which read instantly at 240 px in every frame before the blackout. Keep everything new off it. Also keep all the work done since #102, because the fix is one attribute, not a rollback: the deep-teal marbled field with an eye at the heart of every mandala and the eye-triangles in the pink channels, the hex tunnel and its white-gold core, the woven rainbow spiral eye with its sunburst lashes, the pearl-strung oars, the curling flame fringe that now hugs the whole outer coil, and the two visitors sitting in their discs.

visions.seen: The lights came back on! #121 was still the navy void, and now the whole serpent has climbed back out of the floor of hyperspace with its runes glowing, the braid twisting down its flank and the tail whipped thin into a spiral jewel up top (Vision 3's whip, taken; Vision 2's braid and star river, taken). But the white-gold sun at the bottom of the tunnel is an empty blur, a door with nobody behind it, and the crest is burning against a wall of mud-brown smoke.
suggestions: **The white-gold core of the hex tunnel, just under the chin** (the bloom centered near x 395, y 495 in the 800 px render, just left of where the two oars pass; halve for the 400 box). The brightest place in the piece has nothing in it. I see someone at the bottom of the tunnel looking back up: a small almond eye about 24 px wide in white and pale gold, with a violet pupil and one pinprick highlight, wrapped in a hairline six-petal star of cream (#FFF3C4) at about 85% opacity so the bloom still glows through and around it. Then the woven spiral eye, the tail's spiral jewel and the tunnel's eye make three portals that rhyme. At the end of the breakthrough the light is never empty, it is a presence that sees you seeing it. It stays tiny and sits a good 45 px above the banner's top edge, so the name keeps its calm.

**The murky brown wall behind the crest, upper left** (the flat mud-brown wedge between the flame streamers and the field, about x 220 to 330, y 80 to 310). This is the membrane that joins the streamers, but it reads as dried smoke and drinks the fire's light. I see it turning into lit ember glass: swap the flat brown for a radial gradient that starts hot amber (#FF9A3C at about 55%) at the crest's root just behind the head, passes through deep crimson, and fades to fully clear by the streamer tips, so the field's discs and their eyes show faintly through it, tinted orange. Over there nothing is opaque, everything is glass lit from inside, and seeing the watchers through the flame makes the crown burn in front of the world instead of on a brown curtain. (A different offer from Vision 1's ghost chrysanthemum: this one is about the veil itself.)

**The field discs pressed against the serpent's outer edge** (the ring of round mandalas touching the flame fringe on the left loop, x 0 to 120, y 300 to 650, and those beside the rising tail on the right, x 680 to 780, y 150 to 600). The body is loose and fluid, but the world around it is packed like a tray of coins. I see the discs that touch the flame stretched into teardrops swept along the serpent's direction of travel: about 1.5 times longer than wide for the nearest ring, 1.2 for the next, round again two discs out, each one turned to follow the line of the body beside it, with two or three thin flow lines laid into the coral channels between them, running parallel to the coil. In hyperspace space itself is liquid, and a being that big drags the walls along in its wake. None of these discs touch the banner.
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim, which reads instantly at 240 px; keep everything new off it. Also keep the hex tunnel with an eye in every cell, the woven rainbow spiral eye with its sunburst lashes, the whip-thin tail winding into its spiral jewel, the feathered flame fringe hugging the whole outer coil, the three-strand braid and the glowing runes in their star river, the pearl-strung oars, the green visitor at top center, and the eyes at the heart of the mandalas.

visions.seen: The coin tray melted! The whole field is liquid marbling now, teal and violet ink spinning into whirlpools with eyes riding the current, and the lower oar dips into the tunnel floor and leaves rings (Vision 4's ripples, taken; and Vision 5's packed coins answered by the rebuild). But the little gold dots sit dead still in all that pouring water like rivets on a hull, and both visitors drowned in the rebuild, so the serpent's great eye is staring into an empty room.
suggestions: **The little gold rings with dark centers, sprinkled over the whole field** (about 60 of them, all one size at even spacing: for example the ring of them around the chrysanthemum at top center near x 455, y 100 in the 800 px render, and the scatter down the left edge at x 20 to 200; halve for the 400 box). Right now they float apart from the marbling and never move with it. I see them strung into runs of 5 to 8 beads that ride the centerline of the bright teal bands, 10 to 14 px apart, each run winding about one turn into the nearest whirlpool, shrinking from about 6 px to 1.5 px and brightening from pale gold to white as it reaches the eye of the swirl, with the last bead only a spark. In hyperspace light never sits parked, it pours, and jewels streaming down into the vortices make the marbled field visibly flow and give the eye trails to ride inward. Keep them off the banner and out of the serpent's rainbow halo.

**The pocket right of the snout, inside the coil** (x 520 to 650, y 230 to 400, where four almond eyes now drift loose in the current above the round mandala near x 588, y 407). The rebuild washed away the green visitor at top center and the purple one that met the fish face to face, so the snout points at nobody. I see the being re-forming out of the marbling itself: two of those eyes set level, about 45 px apart near (588, 300), tilted up at their outer corners, and two or three of the teal and violet echo bands bent around them into a tall domed head, its crown near y 235, narrowing to a pointed chin that rests on the top of that mandala near (588, 362). Draw it only with the bands, no solid fill, so it flickers between a face and moving water. The entities in there don't arrive from elsewhere, they condense out of the pattern, and a face you discover in the current is the most DMT thing a loose and fluid field can do. It also gives the oarfish someone to meet again (and Vision 1's drifting glyphs a listener, if they ever want one).

**The burnt-orange ink islands all through the field** (thickest along the left edge at x 20 to 200, y 250 to 450, and around the chrysanthemum at top center). Their edges are crumbly and frayed, like torn paper, and many stop blunt. I see every orange outline smoothed into silk (resample the contour and fit smooth curves through it), then stretched along its local current so it ends in a hair-fine tail, about 0.5 px at the tip, that curls into the next whirlpool. Where orange ink sits within about 40 px of the flame fringe, it could cool toward rose-magenta, so the serpent's fire is the only fire in the world. Marbled ink and hyperspace share one law, that every edge is perfectly liquid and nothing crumbles, and tapering tails make the whole field pour in the direction the serpent swims while the cooled ink frames the flame instead of competing with it.
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim, which reads instantly at 240 px; keep everything new off it. Also keep the new marbled field with its counter-turning whirlpools, the almond eyes and paisleys turned along the flow, the shorter lower oar resting on the tunnel floor with its ripple rings, the hex tunnel with an eye in every cell, the woven rainbow spiral eye with its sunburst lashes, the whip-thin tail winding into its spiral jewel, the three-strand braid and the glowing runes in their star river, and the feathered flame fringe hugging the outer coil. Vision 5's eye in the tunnel core and the ember-glass crest are still waiting, and you've said the crest comes next.

visions.seen: The room filled back up! A ghost face is condensing out of the current right in front of the snout with the marbling pouring straight through its skull, the green visitor is home at top center, and strings of beads spiral down every drain (all three of Vision 6's offers, taken). But dozens of almond eyes in the walls all stare dead ahead at nothing, like a crowd that never noticed the king of herrings swim in.
suggestions: **Every almond eye in the marbled field** (the pink-lidded eyes with cyan irises scattered all over the walls, for example the cluster left of the crest near x 40 to 200, y 60 to 140 in the 800 px render, and the run down the lower right at x 620 to 780, y 600 to 780; halve for the 400 box). Their irises all sit dead center. I see the whole field turning to look at the oarfish: slide each iris and pupil toward the serpent's portal eye (center near x 466, y 332) by about 30% of the eye's half-length, measured in that eye's own tilted frame and kept inside the lid, so the lids keep following the current while the gazes all point one way. Leave three or four of the eyes nearest the badge rim staring straight out at the viewer, pupils centered and a touch larger. In hyperspace every surface is aware, and a hundred eyes turning together is that awareness made visible: it pulls the viewer's eye along their sightlines to the fish, and the few who look back out catch you looking.

**The hex floor of the tunnel, under the chin** (the ellipse of eye-cells inside the cyan bowl, roughly x 200 to 600, y 440 to 580, around the small eye at its core near x 415, y 508). The marbled walls spin and the tail coils, but the tunnel's rings sit perfectly still, like tiles on a floor. I see the descent becoming a vortex: turn each ring of cells about 5 degrees further than the ring outside it (rotate in the round, before the tunnel's perspective squash), so the seams between cells curve into six spiral arms winding down to the core eye, turning the same way as the serpent's coil, and tilt the little eye in each cell to lie along its arm. The bowl's outline and rim stay exactly where they are. The breakthrough is a pull, not a view, and a floor that spirals in makes the sun of the piece rhyme with the whirlpools above and the tail's spiral jewel.

**The big white highlight on the portal eye's violet pupil** (the round glint near x 459, y 324, with the smaller one near x 475, y 341). I see that glint as a reflection of who the fish is facing: replace the big dot with a tiny white silhouette of the ghost face beside the snout, a domed teardrop about 11 px tall, gently curved as if lying on the surface of a sphere, with two dark almond slits for eyes and a hairline gold arc for its crown, at about 90% opacity. Keep the small glint as a plain spark. Over there, when you look into an eye you find the one who is watching, and this closes the loop of gaze between serpent and being without adding a single thing to the crowded field. At badge size it still reads as a highlight.
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim, which reads instantly in the 240 px test; keep everything new off it. Also keep the ghost face made of nothing but lines of light with the current flowing through it, the purple visitor stacked beneath it, the green visitor in its black pocket at top center, the bead runs shrinking to white sparks as they spiral into the whirlpools, the field's rose ink that leaves the serpent as the only fire, the glowing crest membrane with its forked ember tips, the small eye at the tunnel's core, the woven spiral eye with its sunburst lashes, the whip-thin tail winding into its jewel, the braid and glowing runes, and the feathered flame fringe on the outer coil.

visions.seen: The fish is talking! A little string of runes curls out of the snout along a dotted gold arc and dives into the ghost's third eye (Vision 1's oldest offer, finally taken), chrysanthemums bloom all through the walls, and the banner's end lobes have their own quiet night sky. But the serpent's belly hangs right over the sun of the tunnel and stays pale lavender like a dinner plate, as if chrome had never heard of light.
suggestions: **The serpent's pale belly where it hangs over the tunnel** (the whitish lavender band with the gray wavy lines under the rune lane, about x 120 to 390, y 400 to 455 in the 800 px render, plus the underside of the head at x 395 to 470, y 390 to 412 and the inner edge of the rising right side at x 640 to 665, y 330 to 560; halve for the 400 box). Real chrome is a mirror, and this one floats over hyperspace's brightest room. I see the tunnel reflected in it: a strip of the floor's hex cells redrawn as thin cyan, violet and magenta outlines, squashed to about a third of their height and stretched along the spine, bending with the body like a reflection in a spoon, at 25 to 35% opacity under the braid. Right above the core (around x 340 to 470) the strip warms into a soft gold-white smear (#FFF3C4 into #FFD23F, blurred, about 50% at its heart), the core's own glow caught in the metal. Over there every surface is a mirror that shows you the whole world bent around it, and once the belly carries the tunnel, fish and room become one lit place. It all stays on the body, far above the banner.

**The air just outside the flame crown, upper left** (a band about 40 px wide hugging the outside of the crest, from the forked tips near x 230 to 300, y 60 to 110, down its left side to about y 290, and along its upper right edge toward the head near x 460, y 290). The fire burns, but the world beside it sits perfectly still. I see the crown bending space: a copy of the marbled field in that band only, run through a gentle ripple (low-frequency fractal noise, around 0.02 by 0.05, displacing 6 to 8 px), faded in by a soft mask that is strongest against the flames and gone 40 px out, with a faint amber wash (#FF9A3C, about 12%) on top. Then the eyes and bands nearest the fire wobble like a road in summer. In hyperspace power warps the air you look through, and heat haze is the loosest, most fluid way to say this crown is hot enough to bend the room. Keep it out of the green visitor's pocket at top center.

**The dark spiral pockets in the field** (the round black discs holding a cream spiral and a rainbow arc: the one on the left edge near x 35, y 320, the one at upper right near x 715, y 165, and any siblings around the rim). I see the innermost turn of each spiral becoming the serpent itself: the badge's own coil drawn tiny, about 30 to 36 px across, as a 1 px gold line that winds into the spiral's center, with a red flick for the crest and one white dot for the eye. You look into a corner of the vision and find the whole vision again, smaller, swimming the same way, and that endless nesting is the signature of the place. At badge size it still just reads as a spiral; up close it is a secret. (Not Vision 2's turning chrysanthemum: this one nests the fish inside the field.)
visions.keep: The navy banner with the cream neon SavesFish in its pink outline and gold rim, still instant at 240 px, with its new tone-on-tone stars and gold scroll curls kept well clear of the letters; keep everything new off it. Also keep the runes drifting from the mouth into the ghost's third eye, the ghost made of light with the current flowing through its skull, the purple visitor beneath it and the green visitor at top center, the chrysanthemums now blooming all over the walls, the bead runs spiraling into the whirlpools, the glowing crest with its forked ember tips, the hex tunnel with its eye at the core and the oar ripples, the woven spiral eye with its sunburst lashes, the whip tail curling into its jewel, the braid and glowing runes in their star river, and the feathered flame fringe. Vision 7's three offers (the field's eyes turning toward the fish, the spiraling hex floor, the ghost reflected in the pupil) arrived while round 18 was already underway, so they're still waiting too.
